calls.reason: Anthropic describes agents designing experiments beyond coding, while humans set goals. That complicates Marcus's description, but the packet cannot establish his central allegation of frightening readers through a bait and switch.

Anthropic's reports show both harness benefits and model improvements that remove harness requirements. Neither isolates the causes of the June coding gains or establishes the claimed neurosymbolic contribution.
Northeastern's 2022 report corroborates Marcus's advocacy of hybrid models. The technical evidence does not establish that such supplementation was necessary or that his prediction was fulfilled.
Burnell and colleagues describe a gap in AGI measurement, not an assessment of candidate systems. The packet lacks evidence broad enough to establish whether Marcus's definition had been achieved.

Anthropic reports coding and research benchmarks and a possible route to RSI. Marcus's statement about what these results hint at is a hedged interpretation; the packet does not settle their implications for AGI.

Anthropic explicitly says full RSI has not been reached. Its research agents operate within human-assigned problems; their experimental autonomy qualifies the coding-tool description but does not demonstrate autonomous successor development.
